scope: Nine new or strengthened selected-content guides and eleven curation-only paths; curation preserves old history/source/adequacy fields.

profiles.name: Aleut (Unangax̂)
remainingGaps: Extend community-specific coverage beyond the two government examples, including women, families and differing island perspectives; this introduction is not representative of every community.
Read stronger community and specialist evidence for early history, Russian-period change, and Commander Islands communities. The archive finding aid alone does not fill those gaps.
Verify contemporary language outcomes, constitutional amendments, fishery conditions and project status before adding present-day figures or advice.
Review additional camp-specific survivor accounts and the later implementation of redress; the selected memoir and report passages are not full-book reviews.
Seek community review; source quantity and introductory adequacy do not imply endorsement or completed research.

profiles.name: Alsea
remainingGaps: Seek further specifically Alsea family and community perspectives, including contemporary language relationships and cultural practice, without substituting generic Siletz activities.
Read the final1875 enacted provision and the original1865 order directly; a Senate debate is not the enacted law, and authorial summaries can contain chronology errors.
The edited Coos testimony concerns shared reservation history; its witnesses must not be relabeled Alsea or used to fill Alsea-specific depth.
Historical linguistic studies draw on overlapping older corpora. Their analysis and transcription limits do not establish current language use or disappearance of people.
The October2026 coastal-transfer report describes an ongoing transaction. Completion, title and present access require later verified evidence.
Historical photographs are research leads for a later design phase; attribution, rights and cultural context must be checked before any reuse. Community review remains open.

profiles.name: Alutiiq
remainingGaps: Broaden direct family and community perspectives outside Kodiak, especially the Alaska Peninsula, Kenai and Prince William Sound; a regional consortium cannot represent every government or viewpoint.

Investigate provenance between the museum’s Our Stories web text and Imaken Ima’ut before treating them as separate works. Full book chapters and several important scholarly studies remain unread leads.
Review language-plan implementation and present community conditions separately before adding current speaker, population, fishery or regulatory claims.
Seek further oral-history and Indigenous scholarly perspectives on colonial change and continuing cultural life; interpretations of one archaeological site are not regional generalizations.
Historical photographs, recipes and cultural materials have their own rights and contexts. No cooking directions, sensitive places or imagery have been reused here. Community review remains open.

profiles.name: Anishininew
remainingGaps: Broaden community-authored perspectives beyond the selected Island Lake, KI, Sandy Lake and Wunnumin Lake accounts. Do not turn language similarity into an automatic list of peoples or governments.
Verify school opening and transition chronology independently: the community guide labels2020, while Rabasto narrates2021–22and2022. No single exact opening date is chosen here.
Seek current community-directed language and educational research before making present vitality, learner, enrolment or program-outcome claims.

Ariss and Cutfeet’s detailed2011analysis remains unread beyond its introduction after publisher maintenance. Current legal outcomes, treaty interpretations and institutional membership need separate original evidence.

Community place-name archives and interviews have their own authority and permissions. No precise family lands, mapped naming data, restricted sites, private testimony, photographs or practical recipes are republished; community review remains open.

profiles.name: Apalachee
remainingGaps: Read newer scholarship on seventeenth-century conflict, including Lauersdorf’s full article, when legitimate access becomes available. Abstracts and 403 downloads were not counted.

Develop post-1704 displacement and Red River histories through actual original documents and community accounts. Never treat destruction of a mission or older extinction frameworks as disappearance of a people.
Broaden public community accounts of foodways, language, music and cultural life beyond one descendant institution and one dated broadcast, without reproducing restricted cultural or burial material.
Verify present recognition, leadership and program conditions separately before reporting current outcomes, eligibility or services. Undated plans and a 1996 filing are not completed actions.

Archaeological interpretation at San Luis is local and dated. Underlying excavation reports, Spanish manuscripts and the 1688 letter itself were not independently read through the reviewed summaries. Community review remains open.

profiles.name: Arapaho
remainingGaps: Read original treaties and additional historical scholarship before making precise territorial, ratification or legal conclusions. Older university wording is not independently verified legal history.

Broaden public Southern Arapaho and other community-authored perspectives beyond the shared Oklahoma government and two dated apprentice interviews. Northern and Southern institutions remain distinct.
Seek dated educational outcomes and contemporary community priorities without treating an undated program page, a 2006 code or a 2023 interview as current operations or measured success.

The grammar and documentation article were inspected in specified selected scopes. No audio was heard, underlying corpus independently reviewed or full grammar read. Public source access is not cultural reuse permission.

Sand Creek study methods and park planning contribute to public-history literacy; original recordings, individual narratives, casualty totals and sensitive locations remain outside this account. Community review remains open.

profiles.name: Arikara
remainingGaps: Read a substantial community-directed Arikara language textbook, dictionary introduction or documented educational study through legitimate public access, without reproducing narratives or audio.
Broaden direct Sahnish-authored accounts and historical scholarship; a shared-government overview cannot represent every constituent people’s experience.
Read actual primary records for village movement, colonial trade, treaties and dam displacement, preserving their period, authorship and community perspectives.
Corroborate the 1862/1863 movement chronology; do not resolve conflicting dates by pretending sources agree.
Verify present cultural/educational institutions separately, rather than converting undated descriptions or a 2021 visitor listing into current operations.
No community review, contemporary speaker census or assessment of learner outcomes has occurred.

profiles.name: Babine
remainingGaps: Read the full Fiske–Patrick volume and subsequent community scholarship; compare accounts of women’s leadership, law, colonial violence, relocation, and residential schooling.

Follow the Barricade Treaty account into the original instrument, archival correspondence, and community interpretations of unfulfilled obligations. Compare the community plan’s 1905 chronology with the treaty office’s 1906 narrative.
Add more histories authored by individual communities and clarify the wider scope of historical Babine and related language labels.
Check newer community reports for the outcomes of governance, infrastructure, environmental-assessment, and language initiatives. Source quantity does not establish completion.

profiles.name: Beothuk
remainingGaps: Add fuller Indigenous-authored oral-history material and inspect Chief Mi’sel Joe’s published interview and Santu Toney scholarship directly; neither is counted merely because other works cite it.
Obtain a specialist linguistic assessment of recent classification arguments and inspect original word-list manuscripts alongside their later transcriptions.
Verify developments after the 2024–25 museum reporting year concerning final resting places and spiritual belongings; do not infer completion from earlier announcements.
Extend site-specific archaeological coverage beyond northeast Newfoundland and keep competing interpretations of continuity, social organization, and colonial violence explicitly attributed.

profiles.name: Biloxi
remainingGaps: Add more publicly shared Biloxi family oral histories and community-authored accounts beyond the Marksville-centered collection; this profile does not map all descendants or adjudicate other communities’ identities.
Compare proposed pre-1699 Appalachian connections with additional specialist historical and archaeological scholarship. Similar names alone cannot establish a migration route or a people’s identity.

Locate and inspect the more recent Biloxi dictionaries and additional original field materials. The 2011 KU dictionary and some journal downloads were inaccessible during this review and are not counted as inspected sources.
Seek a community-authorized account of present Biloxi language learning priorities. The accessible Tunica-Biloxi language and ethnobotany materials principally document Tunica reclamation.

Thirteen inspected reading sources provide a substantial starting collection, including sources scoped to the shared Tunica-Biloxi government. This is an expanded introduction, not a completed or community-reviewed history.

profiles.name: Cree
remainingGaps: Extend reading through independently scoped Cree communities and languages beyond Eeyou Istchee; this path is not a history of all Cree peoples.
Inspect original institutional records and public community evaluations before extending the Institute’s retrospective or claiming later outcomes.
Add community-directed language, family and historical publications with their own dates and access limits.
Keep the existing James Bay Cree hood as one specifically attributed museum object, not every Cree community’s attire or a present-government portrait.
No current demographic totals, officeholders, legal powers, program availability or universal community endorsement are established.

profiles.name: Gitxsan
remainingGaps: Add substantial community-authored language and local-history publications tied to particular Gitxsan communities and Houses.
Inspect the actual Delgamuukw judgment and relevant scholarship separately before explaining its legal holdings; the two institutional accounts are not legal advice.
Review public education, food systems and lived experiences beyond institutional summaries.

profiles.name: Haida
remainingGaps: Compare community-authored histories across Haida Gwaii and Alaska without treating one government as every Haida community.
Review current constitutional documents and selected maker-led educational works; linked objects and recordings remain separate tasks.

profiles.name: Haisla
remainingGaps: Add fuller Haisla-authored histories and public accounts of particular families and communities.
Inspect original council records and historical scholarship before extending the colonial-policy chronology.
Review public language-teaching materials and their stated use conditions; no audio or vocabulary inspection is claimed here.
The existing Cedar LNG assessment link remains an unread lead in this batch, not a newly inspected work.

profiles.name: Heiltsuk
remainingGaps: Read fuller community-authored historical works and distinct family or village accounts beyond the selected overview.
Inspect dated project reports and underlying research before assessing ecological or programme outcomes.
Verify compressed timeline dates separately; the site’s current legal, area and population statements are not independent findings by this directory.

profiles.name: Nisga'a
remainingGaps: Add fuller Nisg̱a’a-authored historical accounts and distinct village perspectives beyond central-government material.
Follow later language and archives updates; inspect underlying public resources before describing their contents or availability.

profiles.name: Nuxalk
remainingGaps: Seek fuller community-authorized histories and public language resources beyond the visitor-guide selection.
Establish the guide’s precise publication/adoption history; its filename labels it2022_DRAFT and old population totals are not current figures.
Inspect the marine plans and dated programme reports before assessing implementation or ecological outcomes.
Review Q’umk’uts and Snxlhh as individually named community candidates separately, including current preferred spelling and kind; no automatic separate-government claim.

profiles.name: Tlingit
remainingGaps: Review additional Tlingit-authored histories and language resources from distinct coastal and inland communities.
Read further Yakutat chapters and community-directed studies before discussing particular clan histories, places or resource practices.

profiles.name: Tsimshian
remainingGaps: Add community-authored histories from other individually named Tsimshian communities and distinguish their governments and language contexts.
Inspect selected original language resources and public-history materials without assuming a linked app or sign has been reviewed.

profiles.name: Native Hawaiian (Kānaka Maoli)
remainingGaps: A fuller account needs Hawaiian-authored historical scholarship and original Kingdom-era documents, with island-specific histories.
Contemporary family voices, diaspora experiences, health and housing, and the diversity of political positions need stronger representation.
Legal program definitions, current law and recognition debates require separately dated specialist research; the 1993 resolution does not answer them all.
Learning outcomes, restoration results and present program availability have not been independently assessed.

sourceCounting: 7 appended profile-source contexts and 12 same-ID/same-URL card updates, including one excluded duplicate. Shared/reused publications are not globally new works. Identity-only evidence excluded.
provenance: Selected scopes/dates and media-specific creator/source/rights/complete-available-frame limits retained. No private files or full third-party texts published.
